title: Platelet request — approval / appropriateness
blurb: Click the platelet count band and the clinical setting; the engine checks it against standard transfusion thresholds and writes an approve / not-indicated note.
disclaimer: Decision-support output for a trained physician. Thresholds are general guidance (AABB / BSH) — institutional policy and the clinical picture govern. The pathologist remains the final decision-maker.

rules.impression: APPROPRIATE — prophylactic platelet transfusion is indicated for a stable patient with platelets <10 ×10⁹/L.
APPROPRIATE — with fever/sepsis/coagulopathy, prophylaxis up to <20 ×10⁹/L is reasonable.
NOT ROUTINELY INDICATED — above the prophylactic threshold (≥10, or ≥20 with risk factors). Prophylactic transfusion is generally not warranted.
recommendations: Hold unless bleeding or a procedure is planned

rules.impression: Pre-procedure (minor bedside): target ≥20 ×10⁹/L — transfusion indicated to reach ≥20.
Pre-procedure (major surgery / neuraxial): target ≥50 ×10⁹/L — transfusion indicated to reach ≥50.
recommendations: Transfuse to ≥50 ×10⁹/L; recheck before the procedure

rules.impression: Pre-procedure (CNS / neurosurgery / posterior eye): target ≥100 ×10⁹/L — transfusion indicated to reach ≥100.
Active bleeding (WHO ≥2): maintain platelets ≥50 ×10⁹/L (≥100 for CNS or ocular bleeding).
Massive transfusion / DIC: maintain platelets ≥50 ×10⁹/L (≥75–100 with CNS injury); transfuse per the MTP ratio.
recommendations: Follow the massive transfusion protocol; trend platelets/fibrinogen

caveats.text: In immune thrombocytopenia, transfused platelets survive poorly — reserve transfusion for significant or life-threatening bleeding and treat the underlying cause (steroids/IVIG/TPO-RA).
On antiplatelet agents the count may not reflect platelet function — for active bleeding or urgent surgery, transfusion may help despite a 'normal' count.
